Hey Sunny,

Below is the 4hr chart and the 1hr chart. Notice that if you would wait for price to enter the 4hr zone and engulf on the 4hr zone, you would be taking the entry to the far right. But if you wait for price to enter the 4hr zone and then go down to an hourly time frame, you would enter much earlier. In some cases the hourly would give you a few opportunities to enter. If you watched the hourly you would have tried the short to the far left. Then you would have possibly shorted for the much farther move if you got back in on the trade marked with the blue arrows. If you don't take second trades you might have even missed that trade all together.

So my question is do you enter the trades based on the engulfs from the 4hr engulf (or whatever time frame you use).....or do you watch lower time frames as they unfold. So with the 4hr you would wait for price to enter the 4hr zone, engulf downward on the 4hr and then look at lower time frames for your entries at pockets of supply.

author: rexed9999
text:
Hi Chanya,

Sunny doesn't enter a trade as soon as there is an engulf, engulfs happen all the time, in both directions. We need to identify which engulfs are most significant and trade from them.

In that chart most likely on the HTF there was a supply area above the high, price did not want to go any higher and engulfed the last significant demand which lead to a push up to the supply, this shows buyers are no longer in control and we should be looking to short which will be from the origin of the engulfing of the demand.

For price to return to the origin it needs to go higher and so will be engulfing on the move up, we know these won’t be significant as all price is trying to do is each the origin to get in more sellers and push price down.

That’s how I view it anyway but I would like to see Sunny’s response as well.

author: sunnytrader1984
text:
Hi Chanya, Hi Rex

Thanks Rex for answering Chanya's question. Core to looking for engulfing trading is where it happens. HTF supply/demand, SR flips coming from daily, weekly or monthly TFs. These are the areas where engulfings become significant, otherwise like Rex said, they happen everywhere.

If I would say one thing, it would be, try to figure out who is stronger: Bulls or Bears. once you can answer this question, trade setup will become logical. Try to look where are the profit margins, bullish or bearish.

Good luck guys and have a nice weekend.

author: sunnytrader1984
text:
Hi Chanya

Its you who has to decide how much time you want to sit and wait for price to move in your direction. If I would say something, it would be, plan your setup and then trade your setup. Put your SL in place and TP in place. One of them will get hit. If you planned your setup well and you trust your setup, occasional losses will happen but if you good R:R in place, you will come out positive from it.

Answer me one thing, sitting in front of screen and watching price move once you are in the trade, does it help the price move better in your direction? If the answer is yes, then sit and watch but if the answer is no, leave PO and forget it. Check it once the candle is closed, depending if you are trading from H4 or Daily. Untill then go and enjoy your life.

Hopefully this would answer something.

Good luck.

author: rexed9999
text:
Hi Chanya,

All levels are subjective and we will only know if the levels will hold when price action tells us. Why don't you set alerts for HTF zones / areas of interest and when price gets there monitor the price action? Why don’t you look at areas of interest on the Daily and 4H and then watch PA on the 1H, that way you will not need to be at your desk all the time. Once you see the right PA you can set your pending orders and ‘set and forget’. You will obviously need to monitor the trade once entered however if you aren’t able to do this you can always set your target as the first trouble area? Providing the RR is correct.

author: Tracer
text:
Hey,

As sunny says, many (many!!!) times price stops before the source/origin of the engulf, so i find myself many times trading the level below (QM or swap mostly), but keeping in my that my MENTAL STOP is above or below the origin, in case the majority of the unfilled orders are there and not in the mid level. BUT, If the Origin is engulfed, the trade is no longer valid, so exit either with a minimal loss or when price revisits for a manual close (much more dangerous though).

:)
